content.value_statement: Azure Functions projects can fail under load, timeout, or use outdated runtime patterns. This skill provides current templates and production guidance across .NET, Python, and Node.js.
actual_capabilities: Creates Azure Functions patterns for .NET isolated worker, Node.js v4, and Python v2.
Designs Durable Functions chaining and fan-out workflows with status endpoints.
Explains queue triggers, poison queues, retries, and long-running request patterns.
Identifies cold-start, socket-exhaustion, timeout, logging, and thread-starvation problems.
Recommends extension packages, host settings, dependency injection, and HttpClient lifecycle practices.
Guides migration from the deprecated .NET in-process model to isolated worker.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not deploy or inspect an Azure subscription.
Uses placeholder types, services, endpoints, and package versions that require project-specific validation.
Does not replace load testing, security review, cost analysis, or Azure documentation checks.
Covers common patterns rather than every trigger, binding, hosting plan, or language feature.

use_cases.title: Create a function app
use_cases.description: Select a current runtime model and generate a maintainable trigger pattern with dependency injection and error handling.

use_cases.title: Improve production reliability
use_cases.description: Review timeouts, queues, retries, HttpClient usage, logging, and cold-start behavior before release.

use_cases.title: Modernize existing functions
use_cases.description: Plan migration from .NET in-process functions to isolated worker and update related packages and host configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Start a function app
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Azure Functions starting structure for [language] using a [trigger] trigger. Include dependencies, configuration, error handling, and local validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add reliable processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a queue-based Azure Function for [workload]. Include retries, poison-message handling, idempotency guidance, observability, and expected hosting constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a production issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Azure Functions symptom: [symptom]. Consider timeouts, cold starts, thread blocking, client lifetimes, logging, and plan limits. Propose verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a durable architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Durable Functions workflow for [business process]. Define orchestration, activities, parallelism, retries, status APIs, failure handling, scaling limits, and test strategy.

output_examples.input: Create a .NET 8 HTTP function with dependency injection.
output_examples.output: An isolated-worker project outline with required packages, service registration, HTTP behavior, error handling, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Why do HTTP requests fail after about four minutes?
output_examples.output: A diagnosis of the platform timeout with an asynchronous Durable Functions pattern, status polling, and operational checks.

output_examples.input: Process ten thousand images with controlled parallelism.
output_examples.output: A fan-out and fan-in design with activity boundaries, batching guidance, retry behavior, result aggregation, and monitoring considerations.

best_practices: Use current isolated or code-first runtime models for new projects.
Keep network and Azure SDK clients reusable through dependency injection or static lifetimes.
Validate hosting limits, retry behavior, observability, and failure paths under realistic load.
anti_patterns: Do not block asynchronous work with Result, Wait, or Thread.Sleep.
Do not keep long processing inside an HTTP request when status-based processing is available.
Do not hardcode connection strings, API keys, or production endpoints in function code.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers .NET isolated worker, Node.js v4, and Python v2 Azure Functions patterns.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture, code guidance, configuration examples, and validation steps.

faq.question: Can it design Durable Functions workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers function chaining, fan-out and fan-in, activity boundaries, retries, and status endpoints.

faq.question: Does it support production troubleshooting?
faq.answer: Yes. It addresses timeouts, cold starts, socket exhaustion, blocking calls, logging, and missing extensions.

faq.question: Are the examples ready for direct deployment?
faq.answer: No. Placeholder types, endpoints, settings, and package versions require validation for each project.

faq.question: Does it replace Azure security review?
faq.answer: No. Review authentication, authorization, secrets, networking, data handling, and dependency risks for the target environment.
